title: Code file explorer and file icons
description: Adds <CodeFiles>, an explorer with the files of a change in a tree beside the selected file's code, stepping through the files and their highlights like tabs; lineNumbers on it, or on <CodeTabs>, numbers every file, a file read with file= keeps its own numbers through its folds, and a diff whose lines fit half the code switches between Unified and Split as a block does. files fences draw a tree with status letters (added, modified, deleted, renamed, untracked), notes, highlight steps and folders that fold, reading the output of tree, git status --short and git diff --name-status as is. Status words on a code fence give its title bar a badge, and every titled frame shows its file's icon from VS Code's Material Icon Theme, resolved when the deck builds. The README, the writing-slides skill and VS Code snippets document it.

## Retrying moved out of the client into a module of its own

`<CodeFiles>` is an explorer: every file in a tree on the left, the code of one on the right. Use it to walk through a change set; each file is a step, and so is each of its highlight stops. A fence's `title=` or `file=` is its place in the tree, a `files` fence inside adds files without code, such as deleted ones, and a status word after the language gives a file its letter and badge. A `diff` without one counts as modified. The print view shows only the last step's file, so end on the file the headline is about. `<CodeFiles lineNumbers>` numbers every file, and `<CodeTabs lineNumbers>` every tab; a `file=` snippet keeps its numbers in the file, and folds work as in a block, so fold what the change does not touch.

The build reports a line it cannot read, such as a rename without its old path, and leaves it out.

`<CodeFiles>` around fences is an explorer: a tree of every file on the left, the selected file's code on the right. Each fence's `title=`, or the path `file=` reads, places it in the tree, and a `files` fence inside adds files without code, like a deleted one. Status words give a file its letter in the tree and its badge; a `diff` without one counts as modified, or as added or deleted when every line is. The files play in order like tabs, each highlight a step, and the tree follows the step, opening the file's folders. Clicking a file shows it until the next step; an entry without code only shows where it is. Print shows the last step's file. `<CodeFiles lineNumbers>` numbers every file, and `<CodeTabs lineNumbers>` every tab, as `lineNumbers` numbers one fence: a file read with `file=` keeps the numbers of its lines in the file, and a fold skips the numbers it hides.

The tree is as wide as its longest row, and the code takes the rest: 66 columns beside short names one folder deep, 58 when a rename note widens the tree. A `diff`'s signs take 2.5 of them and `lineNumbers` 4.5. `maxLines` works as in `<CodeTabs>`. In tabs and in an explorer, a `diff` has the Unified | Split switch as a block has, when its lines fit half the code: beside the tree, that is 29 columns next to short names and 24 with `lineNumbers`, so only short lines, such as settings or a list, go side by side there.
